title: Continuum: Efficient and Robust Multi-Turn LLM Agent Scheduling with KV Cache Time-to-Live
technique: KV-cache time-to-live pinning across tool calls (cost-benefit TTL from reload cost and queueing delay) + program-level FCFS scheduling

optimized_metrics.evidence: We present Continuum, a serving system to optimize job completion time for multi-turn agent workloads by introducing time-to-live mechanism for KV cache retention.
Continuum achieves better P90 and P95 latency
per-turn queueing delay reduction brought retaining KV cache
balances the benefit of potential reuse against its cost ... need to maintain system throughput for other requests
optimized_metrics.locator: §4.1 (Cost term = lost throughput from pinned memory); abstract 'while improving throughput'

headline_claim.text: Continuum improves the average job completion times by over 8x while improving throughput.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Delay Reduction: Continuum achieves significant delay reduction ...
metric_definitions.notes: 'delay' and 'job completion time/job duration' used interchangeably for a whole multi-turn agent program (all turns plus tool times); reported mean and P90/P95
offered job (agent program) arrival rate; throughput gain read as higher sustainable JPS

metric_definitions.definition_quote: When the next inference step begins, ... must wait in the waiting queue for other requests to free up GPU memory before starting inference. This per-turn queueing delay can accumulate

load_regime: job arrival-rate sweep (jobs per second) with real agent traces (SWE-Bench, BFCL)
tradeoff_acknowledged: pinned KV cache occupies GPU memory and can hurt throughput/other requests if TTL too long; handled by cost term and TTL expiry
hardware: A100-SXM, H100, B200 (up to 4xB200); Company A internal testbed
workloads: SWE-Bench, BFCL v4 web search traces, OpenHands/multi-SWE-bench agents
extractor_notes: Objective is program-level JCT (mean headline, P90/P95 also shown); throughput is secondary improvement. Definition quotes for delay are loose (text interleaved in two-column layout).
